findings.claim: The delta is correctly placed and transactional, but 'SET LOCAL search_path = public, pg_catalog' explicitly demotes pg_catalog behind public for name resolution during the entire remaining superuser (SET LOCAL ROLE postgres) DDL portion of the transaction. Per PostgreSQL semantics, when pg_catalog is not named it is implicitly searched first; naming it after public allows objects in public to shadow catalog functions/operators for all subsequent DDL. This is immaterial for the --full disposable detran_r7_ctg1_a2 rehearsal (fresh postgres-owned database, empty public), but in non-full mode against a legacy database the preflight owner loop (line 87) validates only the nine domain schemas and never inspects pre-existing objects in public, so the hardening is marginally weaker than the implicit pg_catalog-first default that preceded the preflight's own SET LOCAL. 'SET LOCAL search_path = public' alone would yield the identical fix (public becomes the extension/object creation target, resolving the PG18 pgcrypto gen_random_uuid collision) while retaining implicit pg_catalog-first resolution.
findings.fix: Accepted for this rehearsal as-is; do not change bytes before the repeat rehearsal without a new delta review. As a follow-up hardening delta (post-rehearsal, with its own frozen review), either shorten the line to SET LOCAL search_path = public to regain implicit pg_catalog-first resolution, or extend the preflight to assert that the public schema contains no non-postgres-owned objects in non-full mode, and record the chosen rationale in the delivery report.

notes: Independent read-only Auditor review of the frozen readset CTG-0001-C4-OD-V3-APPLY-SEARCHPATH-DELTA-READSET.md and the SQL2 manifest. No shell, no DB connection, no execution, no edits; no DB PASS is inferred or declared. The reported new apply.sh SHA-256 19c078cb… and the single-byte-delta claim are accepted as coordinator-reported governed records (hashing is unavailable read-only); structurally, line 97 is the only deviation from the SQL2-reviewed apply.sh shape, and the manifest preimage 35c2a7f8… matches the readset's stated preimage.

Item 1 confirmed: the new -c 'SET LOCAL search_path = public, pg_catalog' is the final -c in rait_arguments (apply.sh line 97), after the advisory-lock -c and the canonical/owner/role preflight -c, and before every -f DDL appended at lines 98–108 beginning with 00-extensions.sql; all within the single psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q --single-transaction invocation (lines 91, 97, 109). SET LOCAL is transaction-scoped, so no commit is introduced and nothing persists past the single transaction. The preflight text (line 85) is untouched — it still runs under pg_catalog, public with SET LOCAL ROLE postgres, eleven DDL05/DDL14 canonical comparisons under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks, and role/owner checks — and the DDL order is unchanged (closed 49+3 inventory, 19-pre injected before DDL34, DDL20 then enforce/verify last). The fix mechanism is sound: DDL00's CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto now targets public as creation schema instead of pg_catalog, where PostgreSQL 18's builtin gen_random_uuid() caused the collision. The sole finding is a non-blocking resolution-order hardening nuance.

Item 2 confirmed: TASK-0028-V3-DB.md records the rehearsal as FAIL triaged — 18 collected, 8 PASS/10 FAIL, exit 1, first product error apply.sh exit 3 at 00-extensions.sql:1 (pgcrypto/gen_random_uuid under the lingering pg_catalog, public search_path) — and explicitly attributes downstream missing-object failures to the schema not being applied, not to independent protocol-flow verdicts. The spec structure corroborates 18 tests (9 fixed + 5 injected-failure-rollback + 4 qualification scenarios). The rolled-back diagnostic (SET LOCAL ROLE/search_path/CREATE EXTENSION then ROLLBACK) left the database empty and is presented only as diagnosis; bash -n and the 1 pass/17 skipped static filter are expressly declared 'não é PASS DB'. No overreach found.
